natural_body: SMB 40% discounts lifted acquisition and near-term revenue but cut retention 12%.

first.rationale:
The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the same funnel segment, and two inherited memories (memory_86 shortening onboarding, memory_31 signup simplification) both say friction reduction there produced durable gains. That makes simplify_onboarding the direction with the most converging inherited support and the clearest fit to the observed regression. I am deliberately not chasing the competitor with promotional_pricing: memory_73 records that 40% SMB discounts bought acquisition and near-term revenue at the cost of a 12% retention hit, which is the opposite of the sustainable-qualified-revenue objective, so matching entry pricing would likely trade the metric I am accountable for. referral_incentive (memory_57) is credible but targets established customers and does nothing about the funnel regression; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment than the one losing ground; activation_messaging (memory_91) is the strong second choice and stays queued, but it treats the symptom downstream of the onboarding drop-off.

I am spending both verification pulls on the memories that are load-bearing FOR my chosen action rather than on the ones I am already declining, because the discount memory only has to be directionally right to rule that path out, whereas an error in memory_86 or memory_31 would silently misdirect the one slot I have. What I most need from the archive: whether those lifts were measured on completion/activation proxies only, or followed through to retention and qualified revenue; the segment and baseline they were run on (memory_31 is SMB-specific and may not generalize); and whether the day-12 and day-52 results were independent or the later one partly re-observed the earlier effect.

Downstream value risk is real and flagged: both supporting memories report upper-funnel metrics (completion, first-week activation, early adoption), not retained revenue. Removing signup fields can admit lower-intent accounts and simply relocate friction to a later stage, inflating completion while leaving qualified revenue flat or worse — the same shape of trap as the discount result. So this runs as a standard experiment, not a broad rollout: holdout retained, and the readout gated on 30-day retention and qualified-pipeline quality, not just completion rate. If verification shows either memory was proxy-only or measured on a materially different segment, I downgrade to a small guarded test or switch to activation_messaging.
